before.title: Polestar 2 12V Auxiliary Battery Drain
before.description: Polestar 2 reports 12V auxiliary battery drain during long parking, particularly when "Always-on Connectivity" features (Polestar app + remote diagnostics) are enabled. Pattern shared with sister Volvo XC40 Recharge. Multiple software updates have improved parasitic draw.
before.solution: Update software via OTA or Polestar Space. Use a 12V battery maintainer for storage stretches over 2 weeks. AGM 12V replacement under warranty for documented failures; out-of-warranty €180-€280 + coding.

proposal.title: Polestar 2 12V Auxiliary Battery Drain
proposal.description: The frozen page has no citation and attributes 12-volt discharge across every 2020-2024 Polestar 2 to always-on connectivity, a shared Volvo pattern and software-related parasitic draw. Polestar guidance instead says a discharged 12-volt battery can have several causes, and the reviewed service corpus contains battery testing and maintenance procedures rather than an exact five-year connectivity-caused defect population. The battery, DC-to-DC charging path, sleep current, wake sources, software state and high-voltage state remain separate diagnostic paths.
proposal.solution: If the vehicle is unresponsive, follow the current Polestar manual for safe 12-volt assistance and do not connect to the traction battery. Record the parking duration, warnings and recent charging or software events; test battery state and capacity, charging voltage, sleep current, fuses, wake sources and related DTCs before choosing a repair. Confirm the exact battery specification, replacement procedure and any software or registration requirement by VIN. Do not buy a battery, maintainer, DC-to-DC converter or connectivity module from this page; the failed path and fitment are not established.

before.title: Polestar 2 Android Automotive Infotainment Bugs
before.description: Polestar 2 was the first car to launch with Google's Android Automotive OS native (not Android Auto projection). Owners report glitches: Google Maps freezes, Spotify audio drops, Assistant unresponsive, voice commands ignored, app crashes after OTA. Most resolve with later software, but pattern is ongoing.
before.solution: Apply latest OTA. Hard-reset: hold both lower-corner buttons of center screen for 20 seconds. Persistent issues may need a "system reset" at Polestar Space (does not erase saved profile).

proposal.title: Polestar 2 Android Automotive Infotainment Bugs
proposal.description: Polestar technical journal 36086 documents general infotainment-head-unit concerns for Polestar 2 type 534 from model year 2021 onward, including voice control, navigation, radio, speakers and USB. It does not establish the frozen 2020-2024 frequency claim or every named Google Maps, Spotify, Assistant and app-crash symptom. The frozen reset instruction is also wrong: the journal specifies holding the HOME button below the center display for about 20 seconds, not both lower-corner buttons.
proposal.solution: Park safely before interacting with the display. Record the software version, connectivity state, app and exact symptom; apply an available Polestar software update and use the current manual or technical-journal restart procedure by holding the HOME button below the center display for about 20 seconds. If the concern remains or the display affects safety functions, contact Polestar support for diagnosis rather than assuming that a broad system reset preserves every profile or setting. Do not buy a display, infotainment head unit, connectivity module or control module from this page; software, app, network, power and hardware causes remain unresolved.
symptoms: affected app or infotainment function recorded
manufacturer HOME-button restart used while parked
affectedSystems: infotainment head unit and center display

before.title: Polestar 2 BMS Software Recall — Charge Limit Mis-Reporting
before.description: Polestar issued multiple software recalls for the battery management system (BMS) in early Polestar 2 cars — symptoms varied but included incorrect state-of-charge display, premature regen disable, and charging session terminating early. NHTSA recall 23V-101 (and earlier software actions) addressed several variants.
before.solution: Software update via OTA addresses most BMS recalls. Verify your VIN is current on recalls at Polestar Space or via NHTSA lookup. If charge level is suspect, plug in to an L2 charger and let the car re-baseline.

proposal.title: Polestar 2 BMS Software Recall — Charge Limit Mis-Reporting
proposal.description: The frozen page cites NHTSA recall 23V-101 for charge-limit mis-reporting, regenerative-braking disable and early charging termination, but that is not the reviewed Polestar 2 battery-energy-control-module campaign. The exact Polestar campaign is 21V-110 / R10079 for certain 2021-2022 vehicles: a microprocessor reset could open the high-voltage contactors and cause a loss of propulsion. Its report does not establish the frozen charge-limit or re-baselining identity, and the frozen 2020 year is outside that campaign.
proposal.solution: Check the VIN in the official recall lookup and make sure campaign 21V-110 / R10079 and later applicable campaigns are complete. If a propulsion warning or loss of drive occurs, use remaining control to move out of traffic when safe, stop in a safe location and obtain roadside or qualified high-voltage service. Record state of charge, messages, charging behavior and DTCs, but do not treat an L2 charging session as a recall remedy or battery re-baseline cure. Do not buy a BECM, battery module, contactor or charging component from this page; the frozen recall identity is incorrect and VIN-specific diagnosis is required.

propulsion warning and loss-of-drive safety response prioritized

before.title: Polestar 2 Charge Port Door Stuck / Latch Failure
before.description: Polestar 2 charge port door — operated by the small button on the door — can stick, particularly in cold weather or after debris collection in the latch mechanism. Some VINs received TSB action for revised latch hardware.
before.solution: Emergency release procedure documented in owner manual (manual cable behind sidewall trim in cargo area). Replacement latch assembly $200-$400 + install. Polestar Space covers under warranty for documented failures.

proposal.title: Polestar 2 Charge Port Door Stuck / Latch Failure
proposal.description: The frozen page has no citation for a 2020-2024 charge-port-door latch-failure population, cold-weather mechanism or revised-latch bulletin. Its emergency instruction conflates two different components: Polestar documents an emergency handle that releases a locked charging cable after charging has stopped, and notes that some vehicles do not have the handle; that procedure is not a manual release for the charge-port door.
proposal.solution: First identify whether the door will not open, the door will not stay closed, or the charging cable remains locked. Stop charging before attempting cable release. Follow the current manual only for a locked cable and only if the vehicle is equipped with the emergency handle; do not use that handle as a charge-door procedure. Inspect accessible ice, debris, alignment and the door button without forcing painted or energized parts, then have the latch, actuator, cable lock, wiring and software diagnosed. Do not buy a door latch, actuator, cable lock or charge inlet from this page; the failed component and VIN fitment are not established.

before.title: Polestar 2 HV Coolant Heater (PTC) Failure
before.description: Pre-heat-pump Polestar 2 (2021-2022, before the 2023+ heat pump option) used a PTC resistive HV coolant heater that has documented failure cases — symptoms include no cabin heat, charging-related thermal warnings, and reduced winter range. Polestar covers under warranty.
before.solution: Schedule Polestar Space inspection — PTC heater replacement under warranty (8 yr / 100,000 mi for HV components). Heat-pump option from 2023+ is the durable fix; some 2021-2022 owners qualify for heat-pump retrofit (region-dependent).

proposal.title: Polestar 2 HV Coolant Heater (PTC) Failure
proposal.description: The frozen page has no citation for a 2021-2022 high-voltage coolant-heater failure population or for the combined no-heat, charging-warning and range-loss mechanism. Polestar fuse documentation confirms that the vehicle has high-voltage coolant-heater circuits, but component existence is not defect proof. The frozen claims that an eight-year/100,000-mile high-voltage warranty universally covers replacement and that a 2023 heat pump is a durable retrofit fix are not established by the reviewed primary corpus.
proposal.solution: Treat high-voltage warnings, coolant loss, overheating, odor or electrical damage as stop-use conditions and obtain qualified service. For a no-heat complaint, record ambient temperature, settings, preconditioning and warning messages, then diagnose software, 12-volt supply, fuses, coolant level, pumps, valves, sensors, heater circuits and the heat pump where equipped before naming a component. Confirm warranty coverage and any repair by VIN and market. Do not buy a PTC heater, heat pump, coolant pump, valve or sensor from this page; the failed path, high-voltage procedure and fitment are unresolved.

before.title: Polestar 2 Front Inverter Recall (Capacitor Tin-Plating Defect) — Sudden Power Loss
before.description: Polestar announced a global recall in late October 2020 for early-production 2021 Polestar 2 vehicles — approximately 4,586 globally — to replace a defective front inverter. Terminals of capacitors within the inverter module had defective tin-plating, allowing short-circuiting and sudden loss of propulsion with warning lights. The failure is sudden, with little advance warning, and leaves the vehicle without drive — a safety risk in traffic.
before.solution: Free recall remedy at Polestar Space — inverter module replacement with non-affected unit in a single workshop visit. Confirm VIN via Polestar customer service or NHTSA recall lookup. If you experience sudden loss of acceleration, pull over safely.

proposal.title: Polestar 2 Front Inverter Recall (Capacitor Tin-Plating Defect) — Sudden Power Loss
proposal.description: The frozen page identifies NHTSA recall 22V-029 as a Polestar 2 front-inverter tin-plating campaign. The reviewed official 22V-029 owner notice instead concerns Forest River 2021-2023 buses and a programmable-relay power-center fire risk; it is not a Polestar campaign. The complete U.S. Polestar 2 recall inventory does not contain 22V-029, so that identifier cannot support the frozen 2020-2022 years, 4,586-vehicle global count, capacitor mechanism or inverter-replacement remedy.
proposal.solution: If acceleration is lost or a propulsion warning appears, use remaining control to leave traffic when safe, stop in a safe location and request roadside or qualified high-voltage service. Record the VIN, warnings, software version and DTCs, and check the official Polestar and NHTSA recall lookup for campaigns that actually apply to the VIN. Do not present 22V-029 as a Polestar remedy. Do not buy an inverter, capacitor, drive unit or control module from this page; the indexed recall identity is false and the failed path and fitment are not established.
